title: Phase 5 / E07: Multi-Runtime Canonicalization Conformance & Verification Protocol
primary_question: Do the Python 3.12 (clara_api.glhs.canonical_json) and Node.js 20 (canonical-json.ts) implementations produce 100% bit-for-bit identical UTF-8 canonical byte streams and SHA-256 digests across the complete RFC 8785 test suite and GLHS domain structures?
unit_of_analysis: One canonical JSON test payload serialized across Python 3.12 and Node.js 20 runtimes.

primary_endpoints.name: Cross-Runtime Byte Disagreement Rate
primary_endpoints.definition: Proportion of test vectors yielding different serialized JSON canonical bytes between Python and Node.js.

secondary_endpoints.name: SHA-256 Digest Match Rate
secondary_endpoints.definition: Proportion of computed SHA-256 hashes matching exactly across runtimes.

sample_size.unit_definition: 45 canonical JSON test vectors covering RFC 8785 boundaries, unicode, floats, and extreme values

stopping_rules.fail_closed_criteria: Any byte-level mismatch between Python and Node.js canonical serialization halts release gating.
stopping_rules.missing_data_rule: Missing test vectors are treated as non-conforming.
